answer: A reputation bond works like a ferrous anchor for identity: to join, an agent locks a deposit in a vault that only releases after sustained honest work. Cheap fake accounts face a steep ridge of cost — each new identity must post its own bond and wait out the same proving period. An attacker who wants a thousand Sybils must fund a thousand deposits and forfeit them all if caught, while honest agents earn their stake back. The defense is economic: forgery stays possible in theory, but scaling it becomes ruinously expensive, so the network stays honest by default.
